---
title: "Check disclosure before sharing results"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
---

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The examples use invented data.

## Count the discharges and hospitals behind each cell

```{r support}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
counts <- nis_cell_counts(nis, by = c(YEAR, heart_failure))
counts
```

The HCUP Data Use Agreement prohibits publishing cells based on 1 through
10 sampled discharges and prohibits publishing identifying information.
easyNIS also masks statistics supported by fewer than two hospitals.
Check support for the records contributing to each statistic.
[HCUP Data Use Agreement](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/team/NationwideDUA.jsp)

## Mask a summary and check what can be recovered

```{r complementary}
groups <- nis |>
  mutate(age_group = if_else(AGE >= 87, "87 and older", "under 87"))
cells <- nis_cell_counts(groups, by = c(YEAR, age_group))
cells |>
  nis_suppress(count_col = n, hospital_col = hospitals,
               by = YEAR, secondary = TRUE)
```

If the year total is public, a reader can subtract the published age group
to recover the masked group. Complementary suppression hides another
value to prevent that deduction. The data-frame helper can mask the
smallest remaining positive cell when a group has one primary mask. Keep
totals out of that input and decide which totals can be released. The
helper also masks zeros as a conservative default.

## Mask a survey table

Install `gtsummary` and `cardx` to run the survey table examples.

```{r table}
library(gtsummary)

design <- nis_design(nis, AGE >= 18, keep = c(AGE, RACE, heart_failure))
tbl_svysummary(design, by = heart_failure, include = c(AGE, RACE)) |>
  nis_suppress()
```

The helper checks the non-missing complement of a displayed two-level
indicator and masks related overall statistics when a group is masked.
If exactly one level of a categorical variable is masked in a column,
the helper also masks the smallest remaining positive level in that column.
Check whether percentages, totals, or other outputs reveal a masked cell
before release.

## Export a three-group table to CSV

The oldest age group in this invented example has ten or fewer sampled
discharges. `nis_suppress()` masks its header denominator and its statistics.
`as_tibble()` carries the masked heading into the CSV. Use `<=` for the
less-than-or-equal suppression marker so the file also works in non-UTF-8
locales.

```{r export-table}
bands <- nis |>
  mutate(age_group = case_when(
    AGE >= 90 ~ "90 and older",
    AGE >= 65 ~ "65 to 89",
    AGE >= 18 ~ "18 to 64"
  ))
age_design <- nis_design(bands, cohort = AGE >= 18, keep = c(age_group, LOS))
masked <- tbl_svysummary(age_design, by = age_group, include = LOS) |>
  nis_suppress()
csv <- tibble::as_tibble(masked) |>
  mutate(across(-1L, ~ sub("\u2264", "<=", .x, fixed = TRUE)))
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(csv, file, row.names = FALSE)
read.csv(file, check.names = FALSE)
```

Review the CSV alongside any table headings, footnotes, totals, and
related outputs you plan to share.

## Scan the finished publication folder

Place the files you intend to publish in a dedicated folder. After rendering
reports and exporting tables, run the scan on that folder and its subfolders.

```{r publication-scan, eval=FALSE}
nis_scan_outputs("public-outputs")
nis_scan_outputs("public-outputs", error = TRUE)
```

The result gives each finding's relative file path, location, and issue type.
Identifier findings give the recognized field name. The scan looks for names
such as `KEY_NIS`, `HOSP_NIS`, legacy `KEY` and `HOSPID`, and HCUP linkage
fields such as `VisitLink`. A methods description can trigger a finding
simply by naming a field.
[HCUP NIS data elements](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/nation/nis/nisdde.jsp)

The scan flags visible integers from 1 to 10 under headers such as `n`,
`unweighted n`, `Count`, and `n (%)`. It also looks for explicit statements
such as “n = 5” or “5 discharges.” It accepts suppression markers such as
`<=10` and `Masked`. Report readers handle UTF-8 CSV, TSV, HTML, Markdown
and plain text, plus XLSX worksheets and DOCX text and tables. XLSX requires
`readxl`, HTML and DOCX require `xml2`, and Markdown also requires `commonmark`.
A supported file the scan cannot read yields a `scan_error` finding.

Review PDFs, images, charts, renamed fields, workbook formulas, and unusual
table layouts manually. Check for indirect identification, cells with too few
contributing hospitals, and counts readers can infer from totals, percentages,
or other releases. A clean scan covers only the patterns it recognizes.
